note: Compilação manual a partir de matérias jornalísticas reais (ver `sources`), não de um feed automático. Não há 2º turno para Senado no Brasil: cada eleitor vota em até 2 candidatos e os mais votados são eleitos em turno único.
readme: Brazil 2026 – Senate vote intention, latest poll found for each state (1st round, 4 Oct 2026)
Compiled 1 Oct 2026. Two Senate seats are up in every UF (54 seats); each voter casts two votes; there is no runoff for Senate.
• All 27 UFs have at least one Senate poll (see 'Coverage'). Sheet 'Senador' has one row per candidate per poll.
• Full candidate lists: RJ, PE, BA, RS, SE (Quaest, 20–28 Sep) and CE (Real Time Big Data, 21–24 Sep).
• Leaders only: all other states – usually the top 2–3 candidates, taken from a single summary article (GCMais). ES uses a newer Real Time Big Data poll (leaders only).

• Numbers are NOT on one common basis. Rows labelled 'reduced to 100%' consolidate both votes and sum to 100% (Quaest's late-Sep method and Real Time Big Data). Rows from the GCMais summary report each candidate's share without stating the method, and some states sum above 100% (e.g. Alagoas).

• Evidence of the mismatch: the GCMais summary lists Quaest 8 Sep Bahia as Rui Costa 38%, while the Quaest 20–23 Sep Bahia poll (reduced to 100%) has Rui Costa 23%. Do not compare across the two bases, or across pollsters.
• The 8 Sep Quaest figures are about three weeks old and pre-date the final-stretch Quaest/Globo round; I could only verify the later round for RJ, PE, BA, RS and SE.
• GCMais is a secondary source (a regional news portal). I could not open each underlying Quaest/Datafolha release for the leaders-only states.
• Polls are snapshots, not forecasts. Candidacies can still be changed by the courts.
